html:
A Muslim state in what is now Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, ruled from the old city of Bukhara by the Manghit dynasty from 1785 to 1920. The map shows it in 1880, when it was already a Russian protectorate.

Bukhara had long been a centre of Islamic learning and Silk Road trade. In the 19th century its emirs ruled rich oases alongside the rival Khiva and Kokand khanates, together the Uzbek khanates. Emir Muzaffar fought Russia after it took Tashkent and lost: in 1868 Russia annexed Samarkand and made the rest of the emirate a protectorate. The emir kept his throne and court, and Russia ran his foreign affairs.

The Trans-Caspian Railway reached Bukhara in 1888, bringing Russian settlers and the cotton trade. In 1920 the Red Army stormed the city, the last emir fled to Afghanistan, and the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic took its place under Soviet rule. The map's 1880 shape sits south and west of the emirate's real core.
